reading: Output is a 5x5 grid of 3x3 blocks. The centre 3x3 blocks are the input upscaled x3 (fg cell -> solid block). Each fg cell on an input edge also gets a copy of the input in the outer block just past that edge (corners project on both edges, never diagonally).

slots.core: blocks (1+r,1+c) solid fg colour where input[r][c] is fg
slots.projection: for edge fg cell, a copy of the input in the adjacent outer-ring block (row 0/4 or col 0/4)

why: every output block is empty, solid, or the input; solid blocks mirror the input pattern in the centre, input copies sit outward of edge fg cells
invariants: only the input's one colour plus background

reading: Each vertical bar of 2 has a colour-4 shape on one side and a single marker cell on the other. The 4-shape is reflected across the bar onto the marker side, drawn in the marker's colour.

slots.subject: the 4-cells in the rows spanned by that bar
slots.colour: the colour of the lone marker cell in those rows

why: for each bar, new cells = mirror image of the 4-shape about the bar column, all in marker colour

reading: The grid is split into a 2-region and a 7-region with a full 9 line on one border; 8 noise cells inside the 2-region are erased to 2, while each 8 inside the 7-region is kept and also copied one cell toward the 9 border.

slots.region: colour (2 or 7) that dominates the 8's neighbours
slots.grow: 8 in 7-region: neighbour cell in the direction of the full 9 border line becomes 8

why: only 8 cells and their one neighbour toward the 9 side change

reading: From each 6 on the bottom row a 2-path climbs upward. When the next cell up is a horizontal 7-bar, that bar cell becomes 8, the current cell 4, the path runs right under the bar to one column past the bar's right end (marked 3) and climbs again. The path ends with 6 at the top border (or where it is boxed in).

slots.on_hit: bar cell -> 8, turn cell -> 4, run right beneath bar, exit cell one past bar end -> 3, continue up
slots.end: 6 at top border or dead end

why: every 2/3/4/8/6 added lies on one such staircase path from a bottom 6
invariants: 7 bars other than hit cells unchanged

reading: Four 4-cells mark the corners of a box; inside it a few enlarged colour blocks appear. Output is that box (corners included) with the small multi-coloured exemplar found elsewhere scaled up and placed so it agrees with the enlarged blocks already inside.

slots.window: bounding box of the four 4 corner marks
slots.exemplar: small multi-coloured component outside the window
slots.scale: ratio of an inside block to the matching exemplar cell
slots.placement: aligned with the partial enlarged blocks inside the window

why: output = cropped window with the exemplar scaled by k drawn over it, matching the given blocks
invariants: 4 corner marks stay at the output corners

reading: Count the cells of each non-background colour (each count is a square number). Draw a solid square of side sqrt(count) per colour, sorted smallest to largest from left to right, bottom-aligned, separated by one background column.

slots.items: each non-background colour with its cell count
slots.layout: bottom-aligned, 1-column background gaps; height = largest side

why: each colour's area is preserved as a square; output size = (max side) x (sum of sides + gaps)

reading: Each filled rectangle carries one odd-coloured cell. Its interior is cleared to background and an envelope is drawn in the odd colour: diagonals from the four interior corners run inward until they meet the middle, joined by a straight line along the longer axis.

slots.subject: each rectangle (object)
slots.pattern: 45-degree diagonals from interior corners to the midline, then straight along the midline of the longer side

why: inside every rectangle the only coloured interior cells lie on that X/envelope

reading: Output is 3x3 blocks of 3x3. Each block whose input cell is background holds the colour-inverted input (fg->0, 0->fg colour); blocks under fg cells stay empty.

slots.extent: blocks where the input cell is background
slots.unit: input with fg and background swapped

why: every block is empty or the inverted input, placed exactly at the input's background cells

reading: The grid is three 3x3 panels separated by 5 columns; the first panel is given, the second becomes the first rotated 90 degrees clockwise, and the third the first rotated 180 degrees.
why: panel k = source rotated by (k-1)*90 degrees clockwise

reading: The 8-figure is built from 4x4 tiles aligned to its bounding box's top-left corner; every background cell inside a tile that holds any 8 is filled with 2.

new_rows.name: blockfill
new_rows.datalog:
minY(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
minX(min(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
k4(0). k4(4). k4(8). k4(12). k4(16). k4(20). k4(24). k4(28).
r4(0). r4(1). r4(2). r4(3).
rb(Y, K) :- minY(Y0), k4(K), r4(R), T = Y0 + K, Y = T + R.
cb(X, K) :- minX(X0), k4(K), r4(R), T = X0 + K, X = T + R.
hit(KY, KX) :- cell(Y, X, C), rb(Y, KY), cb(X, KX).
blockfill(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C), rb(Y, KY), cb(X, KX), hit(KY, KX).

why: exactly the background cells of 4x4 tiles (grid anchored at fg bbox top-left) containing an 8 become 2
